name: CpG Island Finder
seoTitle: CpG Island Finder Calculator — Formula & Results
seoDesc: A CpG island finder scans a sequence for windows that are GC-rich and CpG-dense against expectation. Free cpg island finder calculator: enter your values and
summary:
A CpG island finder scans a sequence for windows that are GC-rich and CpG-dense against expectation. It returns gc content of the sequence, cpg dinucleotides observed, observed / expected cpg, cpg islands found and longest island, and the panel shows all of them at once.

By the classic definition an island is 200 bp or more with GC ≥ 50% and observed over expected CpG ≥ 0.6. The arithmetic keeps full precision internally and only rounds what it displays, so the number you copy out is the number the formula produced. Units are stated on every box and in every result, so a figure copied out of a protocol, a datasheet or a chart can be entered without converting it first.

sections.title: The formula behind the CpG Island Finder
sections.html:
Expected CpG = (C count × G count) ÷ N. Observed/expected = CpG observed ÷ expected. An island needs GC ≥ 50%, O/E ≥ 0.6 across a window of 200 bp

The symbols in the formula
SymbolWhat it stands forUnit
CpGa cytosine followed by a guanine on the same strand—
O/Eobserved divided by expected CpG count—
Nnumber of bases examinedbp

sections.title: How do I use the CpG Island Finder?
sections.html:
Fill the boxes you have numbers for; the calculator decides what it can derive from them.

  1. Enter the values you already have. Every box accepts a decimal point and a minus sign; thousands separators are ignored.
  2. The grey boxes are results: they are worked out from your inputs and cannot be typed into.
  3. Press Calculate. The results fill in together, and from then on they follow every edit you make — there is no page to reload and nothing to submit.

sections.title: What does the result mean?
sections.html:
Interpretation is a convention, not part of the arithmetic. The usual bands are:

How to read the result
ResultBandWhat it means
O/E > 1.0CpG-richunusual outside promoters and repeats
O/E 0.6 – 1.0Candidate islandisland criteria met if GC is also ≥ 50%
O/E < 0.6Depletedthe normal state of vertebrate DNA, where CpG is methylated and mutates to TpG

  • About 70–80% of human gene promoters sit in a CpG island, which is why a predicted island is used as a first pass at finding promoters in an unknown sequence.

  • Vertebrate genomes are CpG-depleted overall (O/E near 0.25) because methylated cytosine deaminates to thymine. Islands stay unmethylated and therefore keep their CpGs.

  • Methylation of an island silences the gene beneath it — the mechanism behind X inactivation and many tumour suppressors.

sections.title: What are the common mistakes?
sections.html:
Before blaming the formula, check these — they explain nearly every mismatch:

  • Running the finder on a sequence shorter than the window: every window then fails and the answer looks like 'no islands' rather than 'sequence too short'.
  • Treating a predicted island as a proven promoter — it is a hypothesis that needs a transcription start site or a ChIP signal.
  • Forgetting that GC-rich repeats also score as islands.

faq.a: Historically 200 bp or more with GC ≥ 50% and observed over expected CpG ≥ 0.6. Modern genome annotations use slightly relaxed thresholds.

faq.q: How many CpG islands does a human genome have?
faq.a: About 28 000, roughly one per gene, plus many in repeats.

faq.q: Why is CpG depleted in vertebrates?
faq.a: Cytosine in a CpG is methylated, and methylcytosine deaminates to thymine, so CG slowly mutates away to TG.

faq.q: What does the CpG Island Finder actually calculate?
faq.a: It returns gc content of the sequence, cpg dinucleotides observed, observed / expected cpg, cpg islands found and longest island. Each one is derived by the formula on this page, so you can check any figure by hand.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — and if you change an input, every result updates with it.

faq.q: Why is the answer different from the one in my protocol?
faq.a: Nearly always a unit or a rounding difference. This calculator works in the units printed next to each box, keeps full precision internally and only rounds for display, so recomputing from the rounded numbers on screen can differ in the last digit.
